detailed_description: The IP Address Validator checks a single typed address in the browser and reports whether it looks like IPv4, IPv6, or invalid based on local validation logic. For valid IPv4 addresses it also shows basic details such as class, private, loopback, and multicast flags; for IPv6 it shows the loopback flag when applicable. The page includes a few example addresses for quick testing. It does not perform CIDR validation, geolocation, WHOIS, AS number lookup, or network reachability checks.
usage_steps: Enter one IPv4 or IPv6 address in the input field.
Review whether the address is marked valid or invalid.
For valid addresses, check the displayed type and available basic flags.
usage_examples: Check whether 192.168.1.1 is recognized as a valid private IPv4 address.
Test 8.8.8.8 and review its basic IPv4 classification details.
Validate ::1 and confirm it is treated as an IPv6 loopback address.
Paste a suspected malformed address and see whether the validator marks it invalid.
